root_cause_fix_T1.mechanism: Three claim specs assert a FIXED sentence that ignores the fact value: real_machine_embroidery, satin_stitch and tracking. The first two carry a guard qualifying the value; tracking was the only one without. So tracking='we do not offer tracking' VERIFIED published 'Order tracking included.' as a VERIFIED claim.
root_cause_fix_T1.customer_impact: a false fulfillment promise in bullets, description and A+ copy
root_cause_fix_T1.fix: guard=_tracking_included on the tracking spec, negation-aware, failing closed. No new fact field and no parallel boolean -- the fix belongs at the claim, or every other consumer keeps publishing the false sentence.
root_cause_fix_T1.invariant_pinned: test_47 asserts that EVERY fixed-assertion spec carries a guard, so the next one cannot skip it
root_cause_fix_T1.author_error_recorded: I argued a tracking_included boolean was unnecessary because the dedicated concept was already structured. It is structured but not EXACT: a free-text field has no false state. I had built value binding for ship_from_country in the same commit and then defended the identical defect class for tracking.
root_cause_fix_T1.disclosed_limitation: the guard reads prose, so an unusual affirmative phrasing fails closed and costs a legitimate claim. A controlled-vocabulary tracking field would remove the ambiguity and is the right follow-up.
